T-1 Pre-Print Expectations

Consensus called for $62.18M in Q3 revenue (+47.9% YoY) and -$0.05 in GAAP EPS. Buy-side whisper was $64.0M. Options straddles priced a ±12.38% move ($0.53) on restaurant AI expansion.

T+0 Delivery & Strategic Portfolio Pruning

SoundHound delivered $62.42M in revenue (+48.4% YoY), slightly beating Street ($62.18M). However, GAAP gross margin contracted to 34.09% as management non-renewed negative-margin legacy contracts, trimming FY26 guidance to $255M midpoint while initiating $375M midpoint for 2027.

T-1 Thesis Verdict: MIXED / TRANSITIONAL

The voice AI deployment thesis remains intact with $120M in annualized synergies and $350M-$400M guided for 2027. However, elevated quarterly cash burn (-$95.99M) and contract pruning push sustained positive Adjusted EBITDA into second half 2027.

Forensic Cash Quality & Balance Sheet Fortress Assessment

SoundHound recorded elevated cash burn in Q3 2026 with Operating Cash Flow of -$95.99M and Reported Free Cash Flow of -$97.11M. Non-cash stock-based compensation totaled $61.02M, leading to Forensic True Free Cash Flow of -$158.13M.

• Cash & Equivalents Cushion: SoundHound held $207.58M in cash and cash equivalents as of September 30, 2026. Management reiterated that this capital base provides sufficient runway to bridge the company to positive adjusted EBITDA in 2H 2027 without secondary equity issuance.
• One-Time Acquisition Burn Items: Cash burn in Q3 included non-recurring integration disbursements, advisory fees, and restructuring payouts associated with the Amelia transaction.
• Cost Synergy Realization Schedule: Over $80M of the total $120M identified annualized cost synergies will be executed before January 1, 2027, drastically curtailing quarterly operating expenses.
• Capital Intensity Discipline: Property and equipment additions remained minimal at $1.12M, preserving balance sheet flexibility for cloud model training.
Row 4: Operational Wins, Drags & Earnings Call Q&A Audit
QUALITATIVE & TRANSCRIPT FORENSICS

Operational Wins & Catalysts

  • Robust Top-Line Expansion: Revenue increased 48.4% YoY to $62.42M, driven by rapid customer rollouts across automotive and restaurant verticals.
  • Doubled Synergy Target: Identified $120M in annualized cost reductions ($80M+ pre-2027), doubling previous estimates and accelerating structural margin recovery.
  • Restaurant Voice AI Expansion: Restaurant smart ordering revenue climbed 67.2% YoY to $22.50M as leading QSR brands scaled drive-thru automation.
  • Strong 2027 Revenue Outlook: Initiated 2027 revenue guidance of $350M - $400M ($375M midpoint), reflecting high-confidence enterprise pipeline conversions.

Execution Drags & Watch Items

  • Gross Margin Compression: Gross margin fell to 34.09% (-991 bps QoQ) as legacy low-margin contracts from acquired units weighed on profitability.
  • FY 2026 Guidance Trimming: Full-year revenue guided to $250M-$260M (down from $262.5M Street consensus) due to deliberate contract non-renewals.
  • Pushed-Out EBITDA Milestone: Sustained positive Adjusted EBITDA timeline shifted two quarters forward into second half 2027.
  • Spike in Quarterly Cash Burn: Operating cash flow burn expanded to -$95.99M, necessitating strict execution on announced synergy targets.

Top Institutional Analyst Q&A and Analyst Questions Forensic Exchanges

Dan Ives (Wedbush) — Contract Pruning Strategy & Gross Margin Trough

Question: Can you walk through the decision to exit certain negative gross margin contracts? Is 34% the trough for gross margin, and how quickly does it rebound toward 50%?

Executive Answer: Keyvan Mohajer (CEO): 'When we acquired Amelia and earlier assets, some legacy customer commitments carried negative economics. We made the disciplined decision not to renew those contracts. That creates a minor short-term revenue drag, but it immediately clears our path to sustained gross margins above 50% and positive EBITDA by second half 2027.'

Forensic Assessment: DISCIPLINED OPERATIONAL RESET
Glenn Mattson (Ladenburg Thalmann) — Cash Runway & Operating Burn Spikes

Question: Operating cash burn rose to -$96M this quarter, leaving $207.6M in cash. Do you have sufficient liquidity to reach your 2H 2027 profitability milestone without dilutive capital raises?

Executive Answer: Nitesh Sharan (CFO): 'Yes, absolutely. The Q3 cash burn included one-time transaction fees, severance costs, and working capital timing from our acquisitions. With $80M in synergy actions hitting before year-end, our quarterly cash burn will drop precipitously in Q4 and through 2027. We do not need outside financing.'

Forensic Assessment: LIQUIDITY RUNWAY CONFIRMED
Scott Buck (H.C. Wainwright) — OASYS Agentic AI Platform & Enterprise Demand

Question: How are customers responding to OASYS, and does the shift to a hosted recurring model change your sales cycle length?

Executive Answer: Keyvan Mohajer: 'OASYS shifts us from episodic upfront software licenses to predictable monthly recurring revenue. Our agentic voice models can now perform multi-step transactional tasks—like booking service appointments or processing complex food orders—fully autonomously. Enterprise pipeline is at an all-time high.'

Forensic Assessment: ARR STABILITY FOCUS
